name: The 1975
label: Dirty Hit
lede: Four school friends from Wilmslow went through a run of band names, signed to a label for £20, and kept making the records they wanted: long ones, strange ones, and in 2022 a short, plain one that Pitchfork ranked No. 33 of the year.

eras.title: A run of names before the right one
eras.text: Matty Healy starts in the drum seat and ends up the singer, in a Wilmslow, Cheshire band that changes its name over and over. The 1975 is the one that sticks.

years.h: Healy starts on drums, and the first singer lasts one rehearsal
years.p: Guitarist Adam Hann recruits Matty Healy to drum in a band with bassist Ross MacDonald at Wilmslow High School. When Elliott Williams, the singer they try out, leaves after one rehearsal, Healy takes over the vocals.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, [[George Daniel|22bb3c13-87b5-46ac-8dc9-553b6579c2e6]] later takes the drum stool, which is how the four-piece that still exists took shape. The group plays under a stack of names before settling: Me and You Versus Them, Those 1975s, Forever Drawing Six, Talkhouse, the Slowdown, Bigsleep and Drive Like I Do.

Healy has kept the last one alive. During the 2020 shutdown he teased new music under the name Drive Like I Do.

eras.title: Signed for £20, then a stadium before the album
eras.text: Jamie Oborne's label takes them on, Zane Lowe starts playing the EPs, and Muse and the Rolling Stones put them on the bill before a debut album exists.

years.h: Dirty Hit signs the band for £20
years.p: Healy's words about a pre-owned copy of Jack Kerouac's On the Road, where he found the date that became the band's name. Jamie Oborne's label takes the band on.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says manager Jamie Oborne set up Dirty Hit as an independent label and "signed the band for £20." The name comes from scribbles in Healy's copy of Jack Kerouac's On the Road. Healy recalled: "At the time I just thought that the word 'The' preceding a date was a strong use of language."

Dirty Hit went on to release the band's whole catalogue, often alongside Polydor.

years.h: BBC Introducing plays "The City" off the Facedown EP
years.p: The band's first EP, out in August 2012, puts them on Radio 1's new-music radar.

years.h: Zane Lowe picks up the Sex EP
years.p: The November 2012 EP gives the band its first champion on national radio in DJ Zane Lowe.

years.h: "Chocolate" becomes their first UK chart single, at No. 19
years.p: It leads off the Music for Cars EP, their third, and a video goes up for it.

years.h: Muse take them into Emirates Stadium
years.p: On 26 May 2013 the band supports Muse on The 2nd Law World Tour at the London football ground, months before the first album.

years.cap: The 1975 at Brixton Academy, London, 10 January 2014
years.h: No album yet, and they're supporting the Rolling Stones in Hyde Park
years.p: On 13 July 2013 a band with a handful of EPs plays to a Stones crowd in London.

years.h: Their self-titled debut tops the UK chart on 8 September
years.p: Producer Mike Crossey recorded the sixteen tracks at Motor Museum in Liverpool.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports it was made between June and September 2012 and in March 2013, and that it spawned seven singles including "Sex", "Robbers" and "Chocolate". Metacritic gives it 67/100 from 17 reviews. It reached platinum status in the US, with 1 million copies sold by June 2018.

Gigwise's Ashley Clements called it possibly the best indie LP of the year; Clash gave it 8/10.

years.big: "Glitchy R&B to big 80s powerpop to mid 90s soul"
q: Glitchy R&B to big 80s powerpop to mid 90s soul
years.h: Critics can't agree what the debut is
years.p: That is Matty Healy's own description of the first album's palette, and critics file it under electropop, indie pop, pop rock and emo.
years.xp:
Wikipedia notes that NME dubbed the band's influence on indie pop "Healywave", naming Pale Waves, Fickle Friends and The Aces among the acts influenced.

The band's own list of influences includes Talking Heads, My Bloody Valentine, Ride and Michael Jackson, and Healy names film-maker John Hughes as his biggest influence.

eras.title: Bigger than the bedroom
eras.text: Coachella, the Royal Albert Hall, a social-media blackout, and then a second album with a title that takes a breath to say. It goes to No. 1 in the UK and the US.

years.cap: Healy at BBK Live, Bilbao, July 2014
years.h: Coachella, then the Royal Albert Hall in the same month
years.p: April 2014 brings their first major US festival slot and a night at London's Royal Albert Hall.

years.h: Every account deleted, then back the next day in pink
years.p: On 1 June 2015 the band's social media disappears and breakup talk starts. The accounts return the next day in white and light pink.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the deletion as a publicity stunt. The new look set up the second album, which the band announced that October.

years.h: I Like It When You Sleep goes to No. 1 in the UK and the US
years.p: Singles include "Love Me", "UGH!", "The Sound" and "Somebody Else".
years.xp: Per Wikipedia it also reached No. 1 in Canada, Australia and New Zealand, earned a Grammy nomination for its box-set packaging at the 59th Grammys and a Mercury Prize nomination, and was named NME's Album of the Year for 2016.
play: I Like It When You Sleep, for You Are So Beautiful yet So Unaware of It

eras.title: Sincerity is scary
eras.text: Healy goes to a clinic in Barbados in the middle of the third album, and the record that comes out of it trades irony for plain talk about screens, love and recovery. It wins the Brit.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Brief Inquiry into Online Relationships
yt: Love It If We Made It (Official Video)
years.h: Healy and George Daniel produce A Brief Inquiry into Online Relationships themselves
years.p: They split the work across eight studios in London and Los Angeles, and the record enters at No. 1 in the UK.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says sessions ran from June 2017 to September 2018 and were interrupted when Healy went to a rehabilitation clinic in Barbados for heroin addiction. The record deals with digital communication, recovery and mental health, and critics often compared it to Radiohead's OK Computer. Metacritic scores it 83/100 from 29 reviews.

Singles included "Give Yourself a Try", "Love It If We Made It", "TooTimeTooTimeTooTime" and "Sincerity Is Scary".
play: A Brief Inquiry into Online Relationships
Love It If We Made It

years.src: Wikipedia: A Brief Inquiry into Online Relationships · Wikipedia: The 1975 (band)
yt: Sincerity Is Scary (Live From The BRITs 2019)
years.h: British Album of the Year goes to A Brief Inquiry into Online Relationships
years.p: At the 2019 Brit Awards on 19 February the band also plays "Sincerity Is Scary" live.
years.xp: The record also earned a Mercury Prize nomination, and "Give Yourself a Try" was nominated for Best Rock Song at the 62nd Grammys.

years.h: Greta Thunberg speaks the opening track of the next album
years.p: "The 1975" is a speech by the climate activist over ambient music, released 24 July 2019, and its proceeds go to Extinction Rebellion.

years.cap: Healy at Rock am Ring, June 2019
years.h: They top the bill at Reading and Leeds
years.p: August 2019 puts the band at the top of the festival, six years after supporting the Rolling Stones in Hyde Park.

eras.title: A long record into a locked-down world
eras.text: The fourth album is sprawling and lands in the first months of a pandemic that cancels the tour behind it. Healy and George Daniel spend the quiet producing other people.

years.h: Notes on a Conditional Form is a fourth straight UK No. 1
years.p: Phoebe Bridgers appears on "Jesus Christ 2005 God Bless America" and FKA twigs on "If You're Too Shy (Let Me Know)".
years.xp: Wikipedia reports it was also No. 1 in Australia and No. 4 in the US, and was certified silver in the UK in December 2020. The 2020 tour was postponed and then cancelled during COVID-19. NME named the band its Band of the Decade at the 2020 NME Awards.
play: If You're Too Shy (Let Me Know)

years.h: Matty Healy and George Daniel produce beabadoobee's Our Extended Play
years.p: During the pause the pair produce and co-write the EP, and appear on the No Rome and Charli XCX track "Spinning".

eras.title: A short album, a banned tour stop, a break
eras.text: Jack Antonoff comes into the room, the album gets shorter and plainer, and a night in Malaysia ends a festival. Then Healy announces a break from touring.

years.h: Accounts go dark again on Valentine's Day
years.p: The band deactivates its social media on 14 February 2022 and returns on 1 June with a new era.

years.h: "Part of the Band" is the first single
years.p: Postcards with the tracklist are mailed to fans after the song lands on 7 July.

years.src: Wikipedia: Being Funny in a Foreign Language · Album of the Year: Being Funny in a Foreign Language · Metacritic: Being Funny in a Foreign Language · Pitchfork: The 50 Best Albums of 2022
yt: Part of the Band (Official Live Performance)
years.h: Pitchfork gives Being Funny in a Foreign Language 8.0 and a No. 33 spot for 2022
years.p: Jack Antonoff produces with Healy and Daniel at Electric Lady in New York and Real World in Wiltshire, January to May 2022. It runs 43 minutes.
years.xp:
Pitchfork scored the album 8.0 (Wikipedia and Album of the Year list it as 80/100), and later put it at No. 33 on its 50 best albums of 2022. Metacritic gives it 82/100 from 16 critics, and Album of the Year lists the Guardian and Rolling Stone at 80.

It went to No. 1 in the UK, Australia and Ireland and No. 7 on the US Billboard 200. Singles were "Part of the Band", "Happiness", "I'm in Love with You", "All I Need to Hear", "About You" and "Oh Caroline". It was nominated for British Album of the Year at the 2023 Brits.

years.cap: Healy on the Still... At Their Very Best tour, the Armory, 14 December 2022
years.h: Madison Square Garden, live on Twitch
years.p: The sold-out 7 November show gets five-star reviews from Rolling Stone, NME, the Observer, the Telegraph, the Evening Standard and Metro.

years.h: "About You" goes to radio, and comes back at Glastonbury
years.p: The album track is serviced to radio on 23 December 2022, and the band plays it again at Glastonbury in 2025.

q: We can't let the kids down because they're not the problem.
years.src: Wikipedia: Good Vibes Festival · Wikipedia: The 1975 (band)
years.h: Healy and MacDonald kiss onstage; Malaysia shuts down Good Vibes
years.p: Healy criticised Malaysia's anti-LGBT laws from the stage, and authorities ordered the rest of the three-day festival cancelled.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that Healy and Ross MacDonald kissed onstage and that Malaysian authorities cited remarks against local culture. The band was banned from Malaysia and later cancelled dates in Taiwan and Indonesia; the festival organisers later sued for £1.9 million, according to Wikipedia. Healy said the band's decision to play was a mistake.

Activist Peter Tatchell argued the focus should be on Malaysia's anti-gay laws. Some Malaysian LGBTQ+ people said they feared reprisals, per the Good Vibes Festival page.

years.h: The debut turns ten at Reading and Leeds
years.p: It's the band's third headline slot there, and the set marks a decade since the self-titled album.

years.h: Healy tells Sacramento the touring is about to stop
years.p: At the opening show of the Still... At Their Very Best tour he says the band will take a break from touring afterwards.

years.cap: George Daniel at the AO Arena, Manchester, 18 February 2024
years.h: Manchester's AO Arena show is recorded for release
years.p: The 17 February 2024 night comes out as Still... At Their Very Best (Live From The AO Arena, Manchester, 17.02.24).

years.h: Billboards in Manchester announce a Charli XCX song with the band
years.p: "I might say something stupid" brings Healy and Daniel together with Charli XCX and Jon Hopkins on the Brat remix record.

eras.title: A year off the road, then Glastonbury
eras.text: One show, the Pyramid Stage, and a sixth album with a name and possibly a twin.

years.cap: Healy on the Pyramid Stage, Glastonbury, 27 June 2025
years.h: Glastonbury's Pyramid Stage is their only show of 2025
years.p: Manager Jamie Oborne says in May that it will be the band's only concert of the year, and that a sixth album is in the works.
years.xp: The Guardian's Alexis Petridis called the band "world-class" and the set "hugely impressive", per Wikipedia. NME published the full setlist and set highlights.

years.h: The sixth album will be called DOGS
years.p: Healy confirms the title at Gateshead College and says the band has made two albums.
years.xp: Wikipedia quotes Healy: "It might be one, it might be two... but yeah, we've made two albums."
